scope: Default desktop viewport; real isolated guided runs and all live tutorials. No device/novice-user study.

tutorials.assessment:
Quantitative single-case comparison
The strongest numerical example: a real NISAR change mask compared with an official incident boundary, with close author-output agreement. This is a single-case evaluation, not general burn accuracy.
tutorials.title: Timber Fire, California

tutorials.assessment:
Qualitative event comparison
A reproducible two-date water-candidate expansion consistent with NASA’s floodplain imagery; classification accuracy is unmeasured.
tutorials.title: Chókwè flood, Mozambique

tutorials.assessment:
Method adaptation with tide context
A historical HH/HV wetland rule transferred to six NISAR observations, with descriptive nearby-gauge association; no pixel-level inundation accuracy is established.
tutorials.title: Wheeler Marsh, Connecticut

tutorials.assessment:
Qualitative motion-pattern comparison
The fitted relative LOS pattern is consistent with NASA’s illustration over matching dates; no independent displacement grid establishes geodetic accuracy.
tutorials.title: Mexico City, Mexico

tutorials.assessment:
Qualitative event-interval comparison
An event-bracketing LOS mosaic reproduces broad deformation patterns; overlap checks describe internal consistency, not independent displacement accuracy.
tutorials.title: Venezuela earthquake sequence

tutorials.assessment:
Qualitative scattering comparison
The real radar changes are reproducible, but this example does not establish lava detection; seasonal and wetness changes remain mixed with volcanic surface effects.
tutorials.title: Krasheninnikov, Kamchatka

tutorials.assessment:
Conditional velocity-pattern comparison
A geometry-aware, zero-vertical-motion speed estimate has a plausible fast-trunk pattern and similar published range; no matched reference establishes speed accuracy.
tutorials.title: Samudra Tapu, Himalaya

results.findings:
3 · What did this run find?

6 compatible GCOV observations cover 2026-08-10 to 2026-10-09. Regional comparisons use 7,162 common analysis cells (2.865 km²).

Between first and last observations, candidate water gained 0.059 km² and lost 0.068 km² on the same footprint.

Candidate water appears intermittently over 0.732 km² and on every observation over 0.054 km². These are observation frequencies, not continuous wetland hydroperiods.

Classification requires both HH sigma-zero below -14 dB and HV sigma-zero below -23 dB. Native conversion precedes averaging. This paper-inspired rule has not been independently calibrated or validated for this run.
results.limits:
6 · What cannot be concluded?

Observed frequency is not the percentage of all elapsed time flooded. It does not provide flood depth, water volume or validated habitat condition; historical paper accuracy does not transfer to a new run.

results.findings:
3 · What did this run find?

8 real GCOV observations from 2 viewing group(s) produced 7453.00 ha of candidate changed patches within 45228.56 ha of valid land.

Threshold z ≥ 2; patches ≥ 10 ha. Spatial normalization: median 1.9986 dB, scaled MAD 0.3636 dB.

This detects surface-scattering change. Independent fire evidence is required for burn attribution; no recovery or severity is measured.
results.limits:
6 · What cannot be concluded?

Scattering change does not establish fire by itself, burn severity, burned vegetation type or ecological recovery. Case-study perimeter agreement does not establish accuracy for another fire.

A combined HH/HV scattering-change score from separate pre-event baselines for each radar view, plus thresholded candidate patches.

6 compatible GUNW observations cover 2025-10-25 to 2026-01-17. Regional comparisons use 510,464 common analysis cells (3266.970 km²).

Reference uses 2698 identical cells across pairs. Pair network: 7 epochs, 1 connected component(s), 0 redundant edge(s). Read the P04 motion-model status or the other phase tools’ network-model status to see whether reconstruction was supported.

Fitted relative LOS rate: regional median 1.597 cm/year (0.133 cm per mean month), using 7 acquired dates over 84.000 days. Rates are relative to the saved reference, not vertical subsidence.

The dated reconstruction is model-derived from measured pairs. No motion is interpolated between acquisitions. Zero pair residuals in a tree do not validate the result.

results.findings:
3 · What did this run find?

3 event groups (shared physical cells) map 22517.263 km² of the selected region.

Relative LOS displacement median -2.245 cm; p10 -19.176, p90 7.877 cm across mapped cells. These describe this mosaic’s spatial values, not earthquake-only motion or uncertainty.

Inspect per-group dates, references and the source key before comparing this multi-view display with a published map.

Overlapping referenced LOS views differ by a spatial median 0.487 cm and p90 4.620 cm. These are differences between views, not accuracy bounds. Check this disagreement before interpreting a mosaic seam as ground change.
results.limits:
6 · What cannot be concluded?

The pair contains all movement during its interval; it cannot isolate individual shocks, prove earthquake causation at every pixel or map building damage.

2 · What was calculated?

Relative LOS displacement across an event-bracketing interval, or a coverage mosaic of separately measured groups.
